title: Dyck words and the combinatorial meaning of the Catalan numbers
content: The module docstring defines a Dyck word of semilength n (n up-steps U and n down-steps D, every prefix having at least as many U's as D's — balanced brackets / nonnegative lattice paths) and states the headline: Mathlib's DyckWord.card_dyckWord_semilength_eq_catalan counts them as catalan n via a bijection with rooted binary trees on n internal nodes. The entry then lists the value it adds over the bare Mathlib statement: the explicit closed forms, a length-based reformulation, a combinatorial positivity lemma (which Mathlib lacks), and the Segner recurrence read on the counts.

title: The headline count, exposed as the entry point
content: card_semilength_eq_catalan re-exports Mathlib's DyckWord.card_dyckWord_semilength_eq_catalan: the number of Dyck words of semilength n equals catalan n. This is the combinatorial definition of the Catalan numbers (what they count) as opposed to the arithmetic recurrence (the sibling entry catalan-numbers-oq-01). Every subsequent result is a corollary obtained by rewriting the count to catalan n.

title: The two closed forms — and why the division-free one is honest
content: card_semilength_eq_centralBinom_div gives the familiar C(2n,n)/(n+1) by composing the count with catalan_eq_centralBinom_div. succ_mul_card_eq_centralBinom gives the cleaner division-free identity (n+1)·(#Dyck words) = centralBinom n (via succ_mul_catalan_eq_centralBinom). Over ℕ the latter is the honest statement: the popular C(2n,n)/(n+1) is correct only because n+1 divides C(2n,n), which is exactly this identity. Both are recorded.

title: Counting by total length is the same count
content: card_length_eq_catalan reformulates the count by total length 2n instead of semilength n. The predicates 'toList.length = 2n' and 'semilength = n' are pointwise equivalent because every Dyck word has length exactly twice its semilength (two_mul_semilength_eq_length); Equiv.subtypeEquivRight turns the pointwise iff into an equivalence of subtypes, and Nat.card_congr transfers the count — a clean transport rather than a re-derivation. Stated with Nat.card to avoid manufacturing an extra Fintype instance.

title: Combinatorial positivity: a lemma Mathlib lacks
content: Mathlib provides no catalan_pos. Here positivity is obtained the combinatorial way — by exhibiting one object of each size. semilength_nest_iterate shows the fully nested word nest^[n] 0 = Uⁿ Dⁿ has semilength n (a one-line induction on semilength_nest); card_semilength_pos then makes the counted set nonempty (Fintype.card_pos_iff); and catalan_pos rewrites through the count to conclude 0 < catalan n. The witness Uⁿ Dⁿ is the canonical deepest path.

title: The Segner convolution recurrence, read on the counts
content: card_semilength_succ states the Segner recurrence directly on the Dyck-word counts: the count at semilength n+1 is the convolution Σ_{i} (count at i)·(count at n−i). Combinatorially this is the first-return decomposition — a nonempty Dyck word splits at its first return to the axis into an inside part of semilength i and an outside part of semilength n−i. The proof rewrites every count to catalan and closes with catalan_succ. The closing small-case ladder verifies the counts 1, 1, 2, 5 for semilengths 0–3 through catalan_zero/one/two/three (no decide).
mathContext: $C_{n+1}=\sum_{i=0}^{n} C_i\,C_{n-i}$; first-return split at semilength $i$ inside, $n-i$ outside.
prerequisites: the convolution recurrence for Catalan numbers
